events.title: Vandals begin a two-week sack of Rome
events.description: King Gaiseric's Vandals entered Rome and plundered it for fourteen days, carrying off treasure and captives to Carthage. The episode later gave the word 'vandalism' to European languages.
events.html: King Gaiseric's Vandals entered Rome and plundered it for fourteen days, carrying off treasure and captives to Carthage. The episode later gave the word 'vandalism' to European languages.

events.title: Crusaders are let into Antioch by night
events.description: On the night of 2 to 3 June, a tower commander named Firouz let Bohemond's men over the walls, ending a seven-month siege. The crusaders were themselves besieged in the city days later.
events.html: On the night of 2 to 3 June, a tower commander named Firouz let Bohemond's men over the walls, ending a seven-month siege. The crusaders were themselves besieged in the city days later.

events.title: Ojibwe warriors seize Fort Michilimackinac
events.description: During a game of baaga'adowe, a form of lacrosse, Ojibwe players chased the ball into the fort and took it by surprise. The attack was part of the wider uprising known as Pontiac's War.
events.html: During a game of baaga'adowe, a form of lacrosse, Ojibwe players chased the ball into the fort and took it by surprise. The attack was part of the wider uprising known as Pontiac's War.

events.title: Guglielmo Marconi applies for a wireless telegraphy patent
events.description: The young Italian inventor filed his application in London for a system of telegraphy without wires. Within five years his signals had crossed the Atlantic.
events.html: The young Italian inventor filed his application in London for a system of telegraphy without wires. Within five years his signals had crossed the Atlantic.

events.title: Coolidge signs the Indian Citizenship Act
events.description: The law granted US citizenship to all Native Americans born in the United States. Some states still kept Native people from voting for decades afterwards.
events.html: The law granted US citizenship to all Native Americans born in the United States. Some states still kept Native people from voting for decades afterwards.

events.title: Elizabeth II is crowned at Westminster Abbey
events.description: The coronation was the first to be televised in full; some 27 million people in Britain watched, many on newly bought sets. It was a landmark in the spread of television.
